extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reporting exhibitions, shows, fairs, parades, banquets, holiday celebrations, and similar special-occasion news pieces — how to select, describe, and frame material to convey the event and its mood. Emphasis is on description, selection of details, tone, and treatment of speeches within such stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of story classification
rubrics_metrics.description: News stories in this division may be grouped in two classes: (1) those of display, such as exhibitions, shows, fairs, and parades, and (2) those of banquets, holiday celebrations, and other special occasions, such as college commencements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify which of the two classes the event belongs to, since although the subject matter is wide, the method of handling the news is much the same within this division. Classification helps determine descriptive emphasis and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — portray events and bring out the spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim in these stories is not only to portray attractively the events and scenes but to bring out the spirit of the occasion. There is generally a dominant note in all these events, and the effectiveness of the description can be greatly heightened by selecting those details that bring out this note.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and present details primarily for their value in showing the mood of the occasion rather than merely recording incidents. A story that emphasizes the dominant sentiment will be more interesting than one that exhaustively lists events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy as truth of sentiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy in news stories of this kind is not simply faithfulness to fact, but truth of sentiment. Untruthfulness lies in adding fictitious details in an effort to heighten the appeal, and in substituting sentimentality for true sentiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not invent or embellish details to create a mood; avoid sentimentalizing. Maintain factual correctness while conveying the genuine emotional character of the occasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of picturesque and significant phases
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief problem in writing these stories is to select picturesque and significant phases from the large mass of available material, and to reproduce the scenes and incidents with vividness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From abundant material, choose moments and images that are visually or emotionally striking and that collectively convey the event's dominant impression. Ignore incidental minutiae that do not serve the chosen impression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dynamic descriptive treatment (one-impression focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Description is of the so-called dynamic type, in that all of the details are selected with the purpose of bringing out one impression rather than of giving a complete picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose descriptions to build toward a single controlling impression (e.g., jubilation, reverence, generosity). Use selective, vivid detail rather than attempting a panoramic, encyclopedic account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of emotional appeal appropriate to the occasion
rubrics_metrics.description: In descriptions of holiday celebrations an emotional appeal is possible because every festival and holiday has its own particular sentiment. (Examples: Christmas = children's day/generosity; Memorial Day = patriotic reverence; Fourth of July = patriotic jollification; Thanksgiving = feasting.) For banquets and similar occasions the descriptive method in a lighter vein is particularly appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match tone and level of emotionality to the specific holiday or occasion. Invoke conventional associations where appropriate, but ensure the emotion is authentic to the event rather than clichéd.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for pure descriptive writing
rubrics_metrics.description: These events offer one of the few chances in news writing for pure description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take advantage of opportunities for descriptive passages — scenes, colors, sounds, and atmosphere — but anchor them in factual accuracy and the story's dominant note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of speeches and toasts
rubrics_metrics.description: When speeches and toasts are delivered in connection with these events, they are treated like other speeches and are fitted into the story as incidents of the occasion, or, if they are of sufficient significance, they may be played up as the feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include speech content as supporting incident unless the speech itself is newsworthy or central; if so, elevate it to feature status and present fuller quotation or paraphrase. Integrate speech coverage so it contributes to the overall mood or news angle.
